Top 10 Hotels

heroSub: 10 hand-picked hotels in central Korat we've reviewed in depth — from an aparthotel with in-room kitchens and a 19th-floor sky pool, to the city's long-standing 5-star next to a big mall, to a quiet garden boutique and clean budget stays by Save One Market. Prices start at about ฿650–2,100/night.
introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of hotels does Korat city have, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Korat, or Nakhon Ratchasima, is the gateway to Isan that many people use as a stopover before heading up to Khao Yai, Pak Chong, or the Phimai stone sanctuary, and the city itself has plenty of food, big malls, and stays across every price level. What makes choosing a hotel here different from a seaside resort town is that Korat is a city where "driving beats walking" — a good location doesn't mean you can stroll to everything, it means easy access to Mittraphap Road and somewhere to park. Some places are aparthotels with in-room kitchens that suit multi-night stays with family. Some sit right by a big mall like Terminal 21 or The Mall, just across the road. Some are long-established 5-star hotels the whole city knows. And some are clean budget stays in the low hundreds that punch above their price. This article rounds up 10 hotels in central Nakhon Ratchasima we've reviewed in depth — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, with the upsides and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Korat city has no metro, and it's a place where "having a car is easiest" because the sights and malls are spread out. You can call a Grab in town, but late at night public transport gets harder to find. The main artery is Mittraphap Road, which runs through the city center and heads straight out to Khao Yai/Pak Chong/Bangkok. The areas in this article: Mittraphap Road / in-town — the city's main strip, near The Mall · Terminal 21 · Save One Market, easy in and out (Kantary, Fortune, Sima Thani, Zenith, Som-O, B2) · Suranarai / Suranari Road — the old town center near the Ya Mo monument, walkable to the train station (Imperial, Leosor, deVloft) · Suebsiri Road — near the Mittraphap exit, handy for drivers passing through (Hop Inn) · Almost every hotel has free parking, the thing reviews mention most often.

entries.name: Kantary Hotel Korat
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mittraphap Road · Near The Mall · Train station 1.8 km
entries.addr: 899/1 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: If there's one hotel in Korat city that multi-night guests agree on most, many reviews give it to Kantary Hotel Korat — a 4-star part-serviced-apartment in the Cape & Kantary group on Mittraphap Road in the city center. It holds the highest score in this article at 9.3 and has ranked among Korat's top hotels on TripAdvisor. What sets it apart from a typical 4-star is its "little home in the city" concept — most rooms come with a kitchenette, fridge, and cooking gear, starting from a Deluxe that's roomier than a standard room, moving up to Studio Suites and One/Two Bedroom Suites with full kitchens, ideal for families who want to warm up food for the kids or for long-stay workers who don't want to eat out every meal. A highlight reviews mention often is the 19th-floor sky pool with a kids' pool, with sweeping views over Korat that look best in the evening, alongside a gym and sauna. The breakfast buffet earns praise for variety too, and staff score especially high — reviews consistently describe them as friendly and attentive. The location on Mittraphap Road is about 2 km from The Mall and around 1.8 km from the train station, making it easy to get around town or head out to Khao Yai/Phimai, with free parking. Honest caveats from the reviews: the standard pillows run fairly high and firm, and some side sleepers wake up with a stiff neck (you can ask for softer ones), the air-con in some rooms has needed a technician, and the decor leans practical aparthotel rather than photogenic boutique design. This isn't the cheapest pick for a single night, but it's the best value for anyone staying several nights, traveling with family, or working long-term in Korat.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're staying several nights or traveling with family, go for a Studio Suite or above — you get a full kitchen and more living space than the Deluxe. Ask for a high floor for the city view, and if you're a side sleeper, request softer pillows at check-in.
pros: Roomy apartment-style rooms with a kitchenette and fridge, great for multi-night stays
19th-floor sky pool with a kids' pool, lovely city views in the evening
Friendly staff, cleanliness praised again and again (from reviews)
Breakfast buffet with lots of choices · Free parking, near The Mall
cons: Highest starting price in the article — better value over several nights
Standard pillows are fairly high and firm, side sleepers may get a stiff neck
Decor leans practical, not photogenic boutique design (from reviews)

entries.type: 4-Star City Hotel · Next to a Big Mall
entries.name: Fortune Hotel Korat
entries.revCount: OTA around 8.5 · 181 reviews · formerly Fortune Rajpruek Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mittraphap Road · Opposite Terminal 21 (3 min walk)
entries.addr: 311 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Korat and want a stay where you can step off and immediately shop and eat, Fortune Hotel Korat (formerly Fortune Rajpruek Hotel) sits in exactly that spot — a 4-star city hotel on Mittraphap Road, opposite Terminal 21 Korat, about a 3-minute walk across the road or roughly 300 meters. That mall is one of the city's biggest and busiest, packed with restaurants, a cinema, and a supermarket, so guests barely have to plan their meals. Opened in 2017 with 159 rooms, it starts from a 28 sqm Superior with a city view, roomier than a typical standard room at a similar price, up to high-floor Deluxe, a 42 sqm Executive, and Suites. What real reviews praise most is the staff service — friendly, attentive, able to communicate in English, with some guests saying they got an unrequested room upgrade — alongside a breakfast buffet with plenty of choices and a chef who makes a good omelette. There's an outdoor pool, gym, sauna, stable Wi-Fi, and free parking. Honest caveats: the building has been open since 2017 and some rooms are starting to show their age, the pool is small, crossing Mittraphap Road to the mall means using the footbridge/crosswalk on a busy road, and importantly, in 2025 some reviews reported the hotel was partly under renovation, with the pool or certain areas temporarily closed — before booking, ask the hotel directly whether the main facilities will be fully open during your stay. It's best for people coming to shop and eat in town, or for an overnight stopover where you want everything within walking distance.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the renovation status before booking to confirm the pool and main facilities will be fully open during your stay. Ask for a room on floor 9-10 or above for the Terminal 21 view, and try the morning omelette at The Terrace restaurant.
pros: Next to Terminal 21, a 3-minute walk across the road, eat, shop and catch a movie
Friendly staff who speak English, some reviews got a room upgrade
Varied breakfast buffet, good egg dishes from the chef · Stable, fast Wi-Fi
Free parking · Good value among accessible 4-star options
cons: Building opened in 2017, some rooms showing age, the pool is small
In 2025 there were reports of partial renovation, ask before booking
Crossing Mittraphap Road to the mall means the footbridge/crosswalk (from reviews)

entries.name: The Imperial Hotel and Convention Centre Korat
entries.revCount: OTA around 8.6 · over 1,069 reviews · TripAdvisor #4 of 60 hotels
entries.badge: 🏛️ 5-star from the low thousands · Most reviews
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suranarai Road · Near Terminal 21 and Ya Mo
entries.addr: 1137 Suranarai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: When it comes to the big hotels that have been part of Nakhon Ratchasima for years, many people think of The Imperial Hotel and Convention Centre Korat first — a 5-star on Suranarai Road in the city center that opened in 1993 and was renovated in 2007. It has the most reviews in this article, over 1,069, and TripAdvisor ranks it #4 of 60 hotels in Nakhon Ratchasima. The most interesting part is that it's a 5-star hotel starting in the low thousands, around ฿1,000–1,200 for a 27–29 sqm Deluxe, which is very cheap for a room at this level, up to a 56–58 sqm Junior Suite and a two-bedroom Imperial Suite of 109–116 sqm for big families. What reviews agree on most is that the rooms are spacious and the beds very comfortable — many say they slept better than expected — alongside a breakfast buffet that several call "first class," with Thai, Western, and Chinese dishes. What makes this hotel different is its large convention centre that holds up to 1,000 people, a top choice for weddings, seminars, and banquets in Korat for years. There's an outdoor pool, spa, gym, and free parking on a large lot. The location is about 3-4 km from Terminal 21 and around 3 km from the Thao Suranari (Ya Mo) monument. Honest caveats: the building and decor look dated, some carpets and furniture feel original, the design is classic rather than modern, and during big events the lobby and parking get busy. It's best for families, business travelers, and anyone who values spacious rooms, soft beds, and good breakfast at an attainable 5-star price more than a brand-new building.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room that's been recently maintained or refreshed for a nicer look. Include the breakfast buffet in your package since reviews rave about it, and if you want quiet, check the schedule for conferences and banquets in advance and request a room zone far from the function rooms.
pros: 5-star hotel with spacious rooms and soft beds, starting in the low thousands
Breakfast buffet many reviews rate excellent, Thai, Western and Chinese
Most reviews in the article · TripAdvisor #4 of 60 Korat hotels
Convention centre for 1,000 · Free parking, large lot · Near Terminal 21
cons: Building opened 1993, renovated 2007, some carpets and furniture feel original
Design is classic, not modern boutique
During big weddings/seminars the lobby and parking get busy (from reviews)

entries.name: deVloft Hotel Korat
entries.revCount: Trip.com/Agoda/Booking around 8.6 · 349 reviews · formerly deVloft Residence
entries.badge: ✨ New building from 2020 · Walk to The Mall
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Trok Samrong Chan · Walk to The Mall 5-6 min
entries.addr: 75/19 Trok Samrong Chan, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: Picture a small, clean, modern hotel tucked in a quiet lane in central Korat, but only a few minutes' walk from The Mall Korat — deVloft Hotel Korat (formerly deVloft Residence) is a small 3-star boutique of around 60 rooms on Trok Samrong Chan in Nai Mueang, open since 2020 and now a popular pick for budget travelers who want a location next to the mall, averaging around 8.6 from real reviews on Trip.com, Agoda, and Booking. The number-one selling point is that it's a 5-6 minute walk to The Mall Korat, only about 180-400 meters away, which means meals, the cinema, the supermarket, and coffee shops are all within walking distance, no need to call a car. Rooms are air-conditioned with a modern tone, ranging from Deluxe Double, Twin, Family, and Connecting Room, all with a fridge, minibar, tea/coffee maker, and free drinking water. Real reviews agree that rooms are clean, roomier than expected for the price, and the building looks fresh since it only opened in 2020, staff are friendly, and there's a 24-hour front desk that helps people arriving late or leaving before dawn, plus a breakfast buffet and free parking. Honest caveats: it's a small boutique with no pool or gym, it's in the city center near a live-music restaurant so some nights you'll hear music until late, especially Friday and Saturday, parking is limited because it's in a small lane with a narrow access road, and a few voices mention inconsistent bathroom cleanliness in some rooms. It's best for budget travelers, couples, overnight stoppers, and people running errands who want a location by the mall in the high-hundreds-to-low-thousands range.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, request an inner room away from the road or the live-music restaurant at booking, and bring earplugs. Make the most of the walk to The Mall instead of calling a car, and ask about parking in advance since it's in a small lane.
pros: 5-6 minute walk to The Mall Korat, eat, shop and catch a movie without a car
New building opened 2020, clean and fresh rooms, roomier than expected (from reviews)
Friendly staff, 24-hour front desk
Free parking · Breakfast buffet · Prices start in the high hundreds
cons: Small boutique, no pool or gym
In the city center near a live-music venue, some nights have loud music until late

entries.type: 5-Star City Landmark · A Long-Established City Hotel
entries.name: Sima Thani Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mittraphap Road · Near Terminal 21 and Save One Market
entries.addr: 2112/2 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: Mention a hotel in Korat city and one of the first names locals think of is Sima Thani Hotel — a long-established 5-star on Mittraphap Road that has been part of the city since 1990, a venue for the city's weddings, seminars, and big banquets for years, and given a major renovation in 2019, scoring 8.4 from 258 reviews on Trip.com. What sets it apart from newer hotels is its "landmark" feel — a big building, a soaring classic lobby that looks stately, and generous common areas in the style of an older-era hotel. It has 265 rooms ranging from a Superior starting around ฿1,100, up to a 32 sqm Deluxe with a King bed that's the most-booked, to large suites. What reviews most consistently praise is that the rooms are very spacious for the price — the scale of an older-era hotel that gives more space than newer builds — comfortable beds, and good soundproofing even right on a main road. Another long-standing strength is the food — the Tapestry Chinese restaurant is renowned for dim sum and Cantonese cooking, drawing locals even when they're not staying, alongside the Nai-Ruen breakfast buffet that reviews praise for variety. There's an outdoor pool, gym, sauna, massage spa, and large free parking. The location is central, about a 4-minute drive from Terminal 21, around 7 minutes from Save One Market, and near Ya Mo. Honest caveats: even after the renovation some corners still feel like an older-era hotel, some common-area carpets are starting to age, the pool has no poolside bar, and during big weddings/seminars the common areas get busy. It's best for people on business, attending seminars/weddings, or stopping over before Khao Yai/Phimai who like spacious rooms with a classic feel and value food and service.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room in the 2019-renovated section if freshness matters to you. Don't miss the Tapestry Chinese restaurant, open to outside diners, and book with breakfast at Nai-Ruen included since it's better value for families.
pros: Very spacious rooms for the price, comfortable beds, good soundproofing (from reviews)
Stately soaring lobby, the feel of a long-established city hotel
Renowned Tapestry Chinese restaurant + varied breakfast buffet
5-star from around ฿1,100, cheaper than many city hotels · Free parking
cons: Building shows its age, some corners still older-era despite the 2019 renovation
The pool has no bar or poolside drink service
During big weddings/seminars the common areas get crowded (from reviews)

entries.name: The Zenith Residence Hotel
entries.revCount: OTA around 8.4–8.7 · 227 reviews · Japanese Zen design
entries.badge: 🎌 Japanese Zen style · Kitchenette in rooms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mittraphap Road · Near Terminal 21 · Walk to Bus Terminal 2 in 15 min
entries.addr: 442/3 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Korat and want a calm, Japanese-toned room with space to cook your own food, set in the city center on an attainable budget, The Zenith Residence Hotel is a name many guests bring up — a Japanese Zen-design residence hotel on Mittraphap Road, open around 2016 with 67 rooms, scoring around 8.4–8.7 across platforms. What sets Zenith apart from a typical hotel is that many rooms come with a balcony, fridge, and a kitchenette with a stove, so you can live almost like in an apartment, ideal for long stays or anyone who wants to cook. The entry Standard Twin/Double is as large as 32 sqm, roomier than the standard rooms at many city hotels at a similar price, and the Suite runs up to 64 sqm. What reviews praise often is that the rooms are clean, the Zen tone is calm and easy on the eyes, and the quiet helps you sleep well, with friendly, attentive service in the style of a small hotel. There's a gym, an Asian restaurant, a 24-hour front desk, and free private parking. The location is central, about 2.5 km from Terminal 21 and around a 15-minute walk to the second bus terminal (Bus Terminal 2), handy for coach travelers. Honest caveats: it's a simple residence hotel with no large pool or resort-style facilities, breakfast is an optional extra that may cost more and is less varied than at a big hotel, the building has been open since around 2016 and some spots are showing age, and rooms facing Mittraphap Road may catch traffic noise. It's best for people working or running errands in town for several days, small families who want space to cook, and anyone who likes a quiet, Japanese-toned atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you plan to cook or stay long, specify a Room with Kitchenette or Suite at booking, since not every room has a kitchen. Check whether the rate includes breakfast, and if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room not facing the road.
pros: Calm Japanese Zen design, clean rooms, quiet and good for sleep (from reviews)
Many rooms with kitchenette + fridge + balcony, great for long stays and cooking
Spacious rooms from 32 sqm, suites up to 64 sqm
Attentive small-hotel service · Free parking · Near Bus Terminal 2

Building opened around 2016, some spots showing age · Road-facing rooms catch noise

entries.name: Leosor Hotel
entries.badge: 🚆 Walk to the train station · Clean, good value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suranari Road · Walk to the train station 850 m
entries.addr: 555 Suranari Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: If you're looking for a stay in Korat city that's affordable, clean, and easy to get to without paying resort prices, Leosor Hotel is a name that comes up near the top — a 3-star hotel of around 72 rooms on Suranari Road in the heart of Mueang district, open since 2015, scoring 8.6 from 91 reviews on Trip.com, and ranked #2 by TripAdvisor among B&B/guesthouse stays in Nakhon Ratchasima. What people mention most is the cleanliness and value — a roughly 24 sqm Superior that many reviews say is cleaner than the price suggests, good-quality bedding, a strong hot shower, and a quiet room for sound sleep. The location strength is that it's only about 850 meters from Nakhon Ratchasima train station, a few minutes' walk, ideal for people arriving by train, and around 1.3 km from Terminal 21. Another plus is the breakfast buffet whose menu changes daily so it doesn't get repetitive, more thoughtful than expected for a hotel at this price, with friendly English-speaking staff, a 24-hour front desk, karaoke, massage service, and free parking. Honest caveats: there's no pool or gym, in-room Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms (better in the lobby), the room decor is fairly plain and lacks character, in-room toiletries and hangers are scarce, and the bedside lamp isn't bright enough for reading. It's best for travelers on business, people stopping a night on the way to Khao Yai or touring Isan, and budget families who prioritize cleanliness and value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arrive by train and it's just a few minutes' walk, no need for a car. If you work online, bring a mobile data SIM as a backup since in-room Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms, and check whether the package includes breakfast — if not, it's about ฿150/person extra.
pros: Very clean and quiet rooms for sound sleep, the best value in the budget group
About 850 m walk to Nakhon Ratchasima train station, great for train arrivals
Breakfast menu changes daily · Friendly English-speaking staff
Free parking · 24-hour front desk · Near Terminal 21
cons: No pool or gym · Plain room decor lacking character
In-room Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms, better in the lobby
Few in-room toiletries/hangers · Bedside lamp not bright enough (from reviews)

entries.name: Som-O House Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mittraphap Road Soi 4 · Terminal 21 about a 10 min drive
entries.addr: 191/22 Mittraphap Road Soi 4 (along the irrigation canal), Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: Picture a small, modern hotel with spacious rooms in central Korat but wrapped in green vegetable plots, where opening the window meets quiet instead of traffic, with a large lot so you can park easily without competing for space — Som-O House Hotel is a small 3-star boutique on Mittraphap Road Soi 4 in Nai Mueang, open since 2016 on a roughly 9-rai plot, averaging around 8.7 (Trip.com about 8.9) from real reviews. What sets it apart is the "in the city but not hectic" location — the hotel sits in a quiet lane surrounded by greenery, yet a few minutes' drive connects to the main roads, about a 10-minute drive from Terminal 21 and The Mall. It has 78 rooms in 5 types, from Superior up to Deluxe, a 42 sqm Grand Deluxe that's airy with a bathtub in some rooms, plus Corner and Connecting Rooms for families. The two things reviews mention most are the large, free parking where you can park easily without circling, and the quiet that makes for easy sleep because it's in a garden-wrapped lane off the main road, alongside rooms that are spacious and cleaner than the price suggests and a breakfast buffet reviews often praise for flavor. There's an on-site restaurant, meeting/banquet rooms, a 24-hour front desk, CCTV, and key cards. Honest caveats: it's not within walking distance of malls or restaurants, there's no convenience store right by the gate, so it suits people with a car better, there's no pool or gym, the room style is simple and understated, and during banquets/seminars the common areas can get busier. It's best for self-drive travelers, couples and families stopping overnight on the way, and people on business who want quiet, spacious rooms, and easy parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It suits self-drivers best — if you don't have a car, budget for Grab fares in and out of town and bring snacks since there's no convenience store nearby. If you want a spacious room, choose the 42 sqm Grand Deluxe, and don't miss the breakfast reviews often praise.

Large free parking, easy to park without competing — the most-praised point
Very clean rooms, roomier than the price · Tasty, varied breakfast
24-hour front desk · Easy drive in and out of town, great for a stopover

entries.name: Hop Inn Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.1 · 117 reviews · Hop Inn group (Erawan Group)
entries.badge: 🧼 Clean budget, score above its class
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suebsiri Road Soi 18 · Near the Mittraphap exit
tags: 🧼 Clean rooms, cold air-con, soft bed
entries.addr: 624 Suebsiri Road Soi 18, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima
entries.storyHtml: If you're driving through Korat and want a clean, quiet, affordable bed with easy parking you don't have to circle for, Hop Inn Nakhon Ratchasima is the most on-point answer in this city — a budget hotel in The Erawan Group's Hop Inn chain, open since 2014, on Suebsiri Road Soi 18 near the Mittraphap exit, scoring 9.1 from 117 reviews on Trip.com, higher than expected for a hotel at this price and second only to Kantary in this article. The Hop Inn brand has a clear concept: focus on cleanliness, convenience, comfort, and safety, cutting what isn't essential to keep the price accessible. Rooms are Standard, around 20 sqm, with queen or twin beds, starting at about ฿770/night. What real reviews most consistently mention is that rooms are clean, the air-con is cold, the bed is soft, and the free parking is genuinely large, easy to park without circling, which is the main reason drivers choose it. There's a 24-hour front desk, round-the-clock security, and free hot drinks in the lobby in the morning. Honest caveats: per the brand concept, there's no breakfast, no pool, no gym, the location on Suebsiri Road isn't by a mall or tourist area so it suits people with a car better, and a minority of reviews say some staff at certain times aren't very smiley. The charm of Hop Inn is its straightforwardness — you know exactly what you'll get before booking, with no hidden costs. It's best for people driving through who want a clean, safe, affordable bed with easy parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's near the Mittraphap exit with large free parking, so it suits self-drivers best — if you don't have a car, budget for a ride into town. There's no breakfast but free hot drinks in the lobby in the morning, and you can head out for Korat fried noodles or rice porridge at a nearby shop.

entries.name: B2 Korat Night Market Boutique & Budget Hotel
entries.badge: 💸 Cheapest in the article · Next to Save One Market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mittraphap Road Soi 15 · Next to Save One Market
tags: 💸 Rooms roomy for the price, 36 sqm
entries.addr: 283/5 Mittraphap Road Soi 15, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima (next to Save One Market)
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Korat on a tight budget, driving yourself, and want a clean bed in the city with good food within walking distance, B2 Korat Night Market is a name guests bring up often in the low-hundreds bracket — a hotel in the B2 group, a Thai budget chain with hundreds of branches nationwide. Its starting price is the cheapest in this article at only about ฿650/night, yet its overall score reaches 8.7 from 653 reviews on Trip.com, unusually high for a hotel at this price. The brand's formula is Modern Minimal rooms in wood tones — clean, simple, and roomier than the price, with the entry Superior as large as around 36 sqm, bigger than the standard rooms at many pricier city hotels, the point reviews agree on most, up to Premier, a Deluxe that sleeps 3, and a Family Suite. This branch's highlight is that it sits right next to Save One Market, Korat's big night market — a few steps from the lobby and you hit food, coffee shops, and souvenirs stretching for what feels like a kilometer, ideal for people who arrive in the evening and want to walk out for something to eat without driving, about a 7-8 minute drive from Terminal 21 and Central Korat. There's free parking right at the door that reviews praise for unloading straight to your room without lugging things far, comfortable beds, cold air-con, free Wi-Fi, and a 24-hour front desk. Honest caveats: it's a budget stay with no breakfast and no pool, ground-floor rooms by the walkway and parking catch some noise from cars and passersby, the standard pillows are fairly thin, cleanliness is inconsistent in some rooms, and it's not in the Ya Mo old-town area. It's best for people driving through for a single night, budget travelers, and people on business in town who want to save and then enjoy Save One Market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, request an upper-floor room away from the walkway and parking — it's noticeably quieter. If you like a high pillow, ask for an extra at the front desk since the standard pillows are fairly thin, and walk the Save One Market next door in the evening in place of the breakfast the hotel doesn't have.

adviceTitle: How to pick a hotel in Korat city to match your trip?

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveler questions about hotels in Korat city

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best hotel in Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat)?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. By score and suitability for multi-night stays, Kantary Hotel Korat has the top score of 9.3 with in-room kitchens. For a clean, high-scoring budget stay, Hop Inn scores 9.1. For a 5-star in the low thousands with lots of reviews, The Imperial Hotel Korat has over 1,069 reviews. For walking to a mall, Fortune is next to Terminal 21 or deVloft is next to The Mall. For quiet, Som-O House is garden-wrapped.

faq.q: ❓ How much do hotels in Korat city cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿650–2,100 per night. On the budget side, B2 Korat Night Market starts at ฿650, deVloft at ฿700, Hop Inn at ฿770, and Leosor at ฿850. Mid-range is The Imperial at ฿1,000, Sima Thani at ฿1,100, Som-O House at ฿1,090, and Fortune and Zenith at ฿1,150. The upper level is Kantary from ฿2,100. All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; during festivals and the Ya Mo festival, prices may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in for sightseeing in Korat city?
faq.a: Mittraphap Road / in-town is the main strip, near The Mall · Terminal 21 · Save One Market, easy in and out (Kantary, Fortune, Sima Thani, Zenith, Som-O, B2) · Suranarai / Suranari Road is the old town center near Ya Mo, walkable to the train station (Imperial, Leosor, deVloft) · Suebsiri Road is near the Mittraphap exit, handy for drivers passing through (Hop Inn) · In Korat city having a car is easiest, and nearly every hotel has free parking.

faq.q: ❓ Which hotels in Korat city suit multi-night stays or families?
faq.a: The standouts here are hotels with in-room kitchens. Kantary Hotel Korat has apartment-style rooms with a kitchen + fridge, a 19th-floor sky pool, and a kids' pool. The Zenith Residence has a Japanese design with many rooms featuring a kitchenette and fridge, great for long stays. The Imperial has a two-bedroom Imperial Suite of 109–116 sqm, and Som-O House has a garden-quiet Connecting Room for families.

faq.q: ❓ Which hotels in Korat city are within walking distance of a big mall?
faq.a: Fortune Hotel Korat is opposite Terminal 21 Korat, about a 3-minute walk across the road · deVloft Hotel Korat is a 5-6 minute walk to The Mall Korat · B2 Korat Night Market sits right next to Save One Market, a few steps to the food zone · while Kantary, Imperial, Sima Thani are central and near big malls but mostly need a short drive.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a hotel in Korat city?
faq.a: In normal times, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is usually enough. But during the Ya Mo festival (late March–early April), Songkran, long holidays, and when there are big seminars/weddings in town, rooms fill fast and prices climb, so book 3–4 weeks ahead or more, especially for popular hotels like Kantary, The Imperial, and Sima Thani. Every platform offers Free Cancellation; we recommend locking in a rate like that if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
